name: Alice’s Restaurant
note: A car and motorcycle enthusiast haven at Skyline and Highway 84, especially on Saturday and Sunday mornings. Meet up, enjoy the cars and stay for great food—save room for dessert; it’s a TougeMap favorite. Gas and a deli are at the junction.

name: Saratoga Gap
note: Skyline Blvd (CA 35) × Highway 9, where the front side becomes the back side.

name: Chevron
note: Popular meetup spot in downtown Saratoga before heading up Highway 9. Sells race fuel.

name: Hwy 9 Viewpoint
note: Parking pullout on the back side of Highway 9, with an overlook and bathrooms.

name: Skyline Vista Point
note: Panoramic views of the Bay Area from Skyline Blvd (CA 35), looking directly out over Stanford.

name: Downtown Pescadero
note: A small downtown with cute coffee shops and lots of character. A lovely place to stretch your legs and grab a coffee before heading back to the coast.

name: Ritz-Carlton
note: The Ritz-Carlton, Half Moon Bay: great ocean views and a place to grab a drink, just off Highway 1 on Miramontes Point Road. Don’t drink and drive.

name: Newcomb's Ranch
note: The roadhouse on Angeles Crest Highway, and the landmark the SR 2 closures are measured from.

name: Rock Store
note: The long-standing stop on Mulholland Highway, at the western end of The Snake.

name: Lick Observatory
note: The domes at the top of Mount Hamilton Road, at 4,265 ft. The road exists because the observatory does — it was graded in 1876 to haul the telescope up by wagon, at a gradient gentle enough for the horses, which is why it turns as much as it does. Visitor centre hours are seasonal and the road is gated in snow.

name: The Cube · Mount Umunhum
note: The concrete radar tower at the top of Mount Umunhum Road, at 3,486 ft — all that was kept of Almaden Air Force Station, which watched for Soviet bombers from 1957 until it closed in 1980. The summit reopened to the public in 2017 with a viewing deck. Gated outside daylight hours.
